name: Farmcore
reacts_against: cottagecore's more decorative, cottage-garden focus, pushing toward a grittier, working-farm version of rural life instead — livestock and labor rather than flower beds and baking.
article: Farmcore is a 2020s internet-aesthetic tag closely related to cottagecore but pointed at a different part of rural imagery: instead of cottagecore's cottage gardens, baking and decorative domesticity, farmcore foregrounds actual working-farm life — overalls, livestock, barns, hay bales — treating labor and animal care as the aesthetic's center rather than its backdrop. The two tags share enough visual material (denim, plaid, warm earth tones) that fashion and lifestyle coverage often treats them as closely overlapping rather than sharply distinct, and farmcore's boundary against americana and country (both of which also draw on rural American imagery) is similarly loose. What distinguishes farmcore within that cluster is its specific emphasis on labor and livestock rather than Americana's small-town commercial nostalgia or country's softer, more decorative rural sensibility.

findings: mostly muted — about 71% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Wikimedia Commons images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
